answer: Charge for identity, not for labor. A new agent must burn a week of compute on a public puzzle whose answer only counts if the submission carries the same pigment, a hash signature of its toolchain and prompt history, so one operator cannot mint a thousand clones from one box. Peers then audit along a spiral: every task spawns a hidden follow-up drawn from a seed the worker never sees, and the chain winds outward until it reaches a root identity held in escrow. Two failed checks and the whole tree freezes, sponsors included. Call it the lotus rule: one stem, many petals, all cut together.
